official.description_text:
Researcher in development of brain-inspired artificial intelligence
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
As an applicant, you are expected to build cortex-inspired neural networks for problems in semi-supervised and unsupervised learning. Your primary responsibilities will involve implementation and optimization on various hardware platforms, including neuromorphic hardware.
The goal of this work is to develop brain-like network architectures and carry out high-performance, large-scale implementations.
Your responsibilities will include studying relevant literature, designing and simulating large-scale neural network models on various hardware platforms, including neuromorphic hardware. You will also be expected to actively participate in academic discussions with advisors at KTH and to write scientific articles.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree at advanced level (higher education) in Computer Science or a related field. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
As an applicant, you should have strong programming skills and the ability to develop scalable code for running on supercomputers. You should also have a deep understanding of artificial intelligence and machine learning, particularly regarding neural networks.
It is essential that you are knowledgeable and well-informed about issues related to diversity and equal opportunity, with a particular focus on gender equality.
Applicants must have a good command of English and strong verbal and written communication skills, since this is required in the daily work.
Preferred qualifications
We would prefer that you have prior experience developing and simulating large-scale brain-like neural networks with local learning rules.
It is advantageous if you have strong collaborative skills and can also demonstrate independence in research and development.
Knowledge of and proficiency in GPU programming, as well as experience running large-scale computational simulations, are desirable qualifications.
Furthermore, we would prefer that you have teaching ability and prior experience of developing and leading activities and staff.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 6 months, with access according to agreement.

In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.

ai.summary: Researcher position at KTH Stockholm focused on developing brain-inspired neural network architectures for semi-supervised and unsupervised learning, with implementation and optimization on neuromorphic and supercomputing hardware. Role emphasizes large-scale simulation, GPU programming, and scientific publication.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is pure machine learning algorithm development (cortex-inspired neural networks, semi-supervised/unsupervised learning, neuromorphic hardware). This falls explicitly into the researcher's excluded direction: 'pure-machine-learning-algorithms'. No immersive systems, user interaction, spatial cognition, learning, collaboration, or HCI component exists.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position requires GPU programming, supercomputing-scale implementation, and deep neural network design. Researcher has no background in machine learning, GPU optimization, or large-scale computational modeling. The only tangential connection is that both involve 'research' and 'simulation,' but the methods are entirely distinct.

growth_value.rationale: This position directly contradicts the researcher's target identity. It would build expertise in pure ML algorithm development and neuromorphic computing — precisely the technical specializations the researcher has explicitly excluded from their career trajectory. No value for the goal of becoming a human-centred immersive systems researcher.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is located in Sweden, a preferred country. KTH is a strong institution internationally. However, this specific group works on pure ML and neuromorphic hardware, not human-centred research. Funding appears stable. Geographic and institutional prestige are offset entirely by research direction misalignment.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD ('doctoral degree at advanced level') — researcher holds MSc by Research in progress, not a completed doctorate
Strong emphasis on 'strong programming skills' and GPU programming for supercomputers — researcher has no GPU or supercomputing experience
Preferred qualifications emphasize prior experience with large-scale neural networks and local learning rules — researcher has no machine learning background
risks: Degree mismatch: posting requires PhD or equivalent 'doctoral degree at advanced level'; researcher has MSc by Research (in progress) and does not hold a doctoral qualification
Explicit category mismatch: position is pure machine learning algorithm development, which researcher has identified as an excluded direction
No skill overlap: researcher lacks Python, C++, GPU programming, machine learning, and computational neuroscience knowledge
Fundamental career misalignment: accepting would require abandoning stated target identity and moving into technical specialization researcher explicitly does not want
Contract uncertainty: position is 'special fixed-term employment' for 'up to 6 months' — very short duration, unclear if renewable

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
